title: Kitab al-Kharaj
author: abu-yusuf
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Abu Yusuf's treatise on the revenue and lands of the caliphate, written at Harun al-Rashid's request. It treats conquered land, the kharaj and tithe, tribute, spoils, the status of non-Muslim communities, and the duties of judges and officials, arguing each point from the Qur'an, hadith and the practice of the early community.
historicalContext: Abu Yusuf was chief judge of Baghdad under Harun al-Rashid, and the book is a working manual for the administration of an empire as much as a work of legal theory. It preserves early Hanafi reasoning and is one of the oldest surviving Islamic prose works on government.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
